title: Embedding service: prefetch + multi-queue scheduler for stable p95/p99
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Reduce embedding endpoint tail latency (p95/p99) for small synchronous requests while keeping throughput stable. Current p99 for single-sentence embeds (avg len 32 tokens) is ~420ms on ded-embed-rt with microbatching enabled; target is p99 < 200ms without regressing throughput more than 5%.

Background: Previous micro-batching improvements reduced median latency but tail spikes remain due to heterogeneous request sizes, kernel launch stalls, and cold KV-cache misses. Work so far improved batching heuristics but we still see sporadic p99s caused by: kernel serialization when multiple small batches contend on the same CUDA context; page faults from host->device transfers; and blocking I/O when KV cache miss triggers remote fetch.

Hypothesis: Combining a lightweight prefetch stage (proactively filling KV cache for queued requests) with a multi-queue scheduler that separates low-latency single-item queues from throughput-oriented batches will reduce contention and amortize kernel setup cost. Additional tactics: pinned memory IO, CUDA stream pre-warming, adaptive batch size per queue, and kernel launch coalescing for small sequences.

Approach:
- Add a prefetch step in the request pipeline that issues asynchronous KV-cache lookups for recent prefixes before batch assembly; if hit, tag request as warm.
- Implement 2-tier scheduler: fast-path queue (single-item or tiny-batch, strict latency target) and bulk queue (larger adaptive batches, throughput-optimized). Fast-path will have higher scheduling priority and will preempt bulk queue when latency SLOs are at risk.
- Kernel-level changes: enable stream-based kernel reuse to avoid reinitializing kernels between tiny batches; tune kernel launch parameters for short sequences (unroll loop thresholds); experiment with kernel pre-compilation warming for the most-used model shapes.
- IO/transfer: use pinned host memory for embeddings input and outputs to reduce H2D/D2H overhead; overlap network KV fetch with host transfers and kernel execution where possible (async RDMA or HTTP fetch in background).
- Adaptive timers: jittered batching timers to avoid synchronized wake-ups that cause spikes.

Deliverables: design doc, implementation in runtime (scheduler + prefetch), benchmark harness for synthetic and production-mirrored traffic, dashboards/alerts, rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback.
acceptance_criteria: 1) p99 on synthetic mix (70% single-sentences, 30% long) measured over 24h in staging drops from ~420ms to <200ms. 2) throughput measured at 95th percentile request rate remains within 5% of baseline. 3) No increase in error rate or OOMs after 48h canary. 4) Monitoring dashboards show KV-cache hit-rate improvement for warm-tagged requests. 5) Unit and integration tests for scheduler correctness and prefetch idempotency exist.
test_plan:
- Microbench: run emb-bench with 10k requests/sec mixed profile; collect p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Production-shadow: mirror 5% of traffic to staging runtime with shadow routing for 24h; compare latencies.
- Canary: gradually rollout to 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic with automated rollback on p99 > 220ms or error rate > baseline +0.1%.
- Stress test: long-run 48h soak with blobbed sequences to validate memory stability.
- Fallback validation: verify automatic fallback to current scheduler if kernel crash or degraded performance occurs.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag off in staging. 2) Merge behind runtime-flag. 3) Shadow traffic in staging (24h). 4) Canary in production on small pool (5%) for 4h, then 25% for 12h, monitor. 5) Full rollout if metrics stable. Rollback if p99 target exceeded or customer-impacting errors observed.
Key telemetry: p50/p95/p99 latency, KV-cache hit-rate, kernel launch durations, GPU occupancy, tail GC/page-fault counts.
monitoring_queries:
Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/endpoint-latency?var-env=prod
Important queries: emb.endpoint.latency.p99{service=embeddings}, emb.kernel.launch_ms.p99, emb.kvcache.hit_rate, emb.gpu.occupancy
